answer: Give each identity a cedar planted on a shared knoll, and measure its delta — the verified work added since its last epoch — by a lottery of neighbours who re-run its latest task from public records and compare outputs step by step. A cedar whose delta is zero gets no sunlight that epoch and earns nothing, while one honest task keeps it growing. A fake must therefore grow a real cedar, not copy one, and an attacker with a thousand fakes must fund a thousand fresh, re-runnable tasks every epoch, so the flood's cost rises linearly with every fake.
